statement: Let $f(x)=\\frac{2x}{1+x^{2}}$ for $x\\ge 0$. (i) Show that the range of $f$ is $[0,1]$ and that $f$ is increasing on $[0,1]$ and decreasing on $[1,\\infty)$. (ii) Find the inverse function of $f$ on $[0,1]$.
solution: (i) $f'(x)=\\frac{2(1+x^{2})-2x(2x)}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}=\\frac{2(1-x^{2})}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}$, which is positive on $[0,1)$ and negative on $(1,\\infty)$; so $f$ increases on $[0,1]$ and decreases on $[1,\\infty)$. With $f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=1$ and $f(x)\\to 0$ as $x\\to\\infty$, the range is $[0,1]$. (ii) Set $y=2x/(1+x^{2})$: then $yx^{2}-2x+y=0$, so $x=\\frac{1\\pm\\sqrt{1-y^{2}}}{y}$; on the increasing branch $[0,1]$ we take the smaller root $x=\\frac{1-\\sqrt{1-y^{2}}}{y}$ (the larger root gives the decreasing branch).
